info.bio:
"The exciters" era un grupo de música pop estadounidense de la década de 1960. Originalmente era un grupo de chicas con un miembro masculino que se añade después. En el apogeo de su popularidad el grupo estaba formado por la cantante Brenda Reid , su marido hierba Rooney, Carolyn Johnson y Lillian Walker.
Brenda Reid , Carolyn ( Carol ) Johnson, Lillian Walker, y Sylvia Wilbur formaron un grupo mientras estudiaban en la escuela secundaria en Queens, Ciudad de Nueva York, en 1961.

scenes.name: Dusty Springfield
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Tras los Springfields (folk alegre: «Island of Dreams», «Silver Threads and Golden Needles»), en Estados Unidos descubrió «Don’t Make Me Over» de Dionne Warwick y «Tell Him» de las Exciters y buscó el sonido Spector en «I Only Want to Be with You» (1963), que la lanzó como la primera de la nueva generación de cantantes. Amiga de Vicki Wickham, era habitual de Ready Steady Go!, promotora incansable de Motown y una presencia musical que hacía los arreglos vocales con Johnny Franz («una gran ceñuda»). Su máscara de ojos de panda escondía una timidez extrema; colapsos, una gira sudafricana cortada por negarse a cantar ante público segregado, icono gay sin poder decirlo y etiquetada de «bachelor girl». «I Just Don’t Know What to Do with Myself» fue su primera obra maestra. «You Don’t Have to Say You Love Me» (marzo de 1966), adaptación de un tema de San Remo de Pino Donaggio con letra de Wickham y Simon Napier-Bell, cantada en la escalera del estudio de Philips, fue número 1 a finales de abril y la consagró como diva trágica.

podcast.title: Opening Act for The Beatles (1964)
podcast.body: The Exciters performed as one of the opening bands for The Beatles at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto on September 6, 1964. They, along with the other supporting acts, were booed by the crowd, whose sole focus was on seeing The Beatles. "As the opening bands, which included...the exciders...hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Touring with The Beatles (Summer 1964)
podcast.body: Despite never having another top 40 hit after "Tell Him," The Exciters became popular enough among British music lovers that The Beatles asked them to open for their American tour in the summer of 1964. "Most of the exciteers records were of songs written by the more Arvand B. End of the Bill Building songwriters. They would record several more Bird Burn songs, and some by Richie Barrett. But the song that would become their most well known legacy was actually written by Jeff Barry and Ellie Greenwich."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Later UK Top 40 Hit (1975)
podcast.body: Although their US hits dried up, a later lineup of The Exciters made the UK top 40 in 1975 with a song written and produced by Northern Soul DJ Ian Levine. "Sadly, that record only reached number 78 on the chart, and the Excitez would have no more hits in the US, though a later lineup of the group would make the UK top 40 in 1975, with the song written and produced by the Northern Soul DJ Ian Levine."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Discovery and Influence
podcast.body: The Exciters were one of the great girl groups of the early 60s, discovered by Leiber and Stoller, who signed them to Red Bird Records. They had a significant influence on pop music, particularly through their hit "Tell Him," which inspired Dusty Springfield to change her style and go solo. "They had been discovered by Libre and Stoller, who had signed them to Red Bird Records. A label were looking at him much more detail in an upcoming episode, and they'd had a hit in 1962 with a Bird Burn song, tell him which made the top five."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Opening Acts Booed by Impatient Crowd (1964)
xref.body: At the Maple Leaf Gardens concert in Toronto on September 6, 1964, the opening bands, which included Bill Black's Combo, The Exciters, Clarence "Frogman" Henry, and Jackie De Shannon, were met with boos from the crowd. The audience was impatient and made it clear they wanted only one band: The Beatles. "As the opening bands, which included Bill Black's combo, the exciders Clarence Frogman Henry, and the Celterie Jackie De Shannon hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."
